00000.notes:
Whenever you sleep, roll 1d6. On a 6, you experience either a Premonition or a Portent.
                                            Premonitions are simple dreams dominated by emotions, sensations, and vague impressions rather than clear images.
                                            After experiencing a Premonition, choose one roll you make during the following day. You receive +3 to that
                                            roll. 
                                            Portents. Portents are true prophetic dreams: powerful visions of events that are happening or are about to
                                            happen.
00000.name: Green Sight

00001.notes: Menkhu (line-knower), not Yargachin (priest) - he has not been cut. Licensed to open bodies and to perform the Kolyarga (the-bog-opening; the lesser rite). Purely social; no miracles. B43
00001.name: Clerical Investment

00002.notes: +3 reactions from the Turchin, and throughout the Neck. Small class of people (x1/3), so 3 levels cost +5 points. The pair is one multifaceted Reputation netting 0. B26-28; People Affected
00002.name: Good Reputation 3

00003.notes: Loyal raven with its own stats, acting under GM control; may fight, scout, track, distract, or carry objects and messages. +1 to melee attacks while it is adjacent and engaged with the same foe. If it dies, the advantage and its 5 points are lost until the GM allows a new bond.
00003.name: Animal Companion

00004.notes: Each night roll 1d6; on a 6 you slip into the raven. Quick Contest of Will: win and you control it (its body, your mind); lose and you only ride along behind its eyes. Return on a Will-4 roll, retried hourly or when someone shakes you awake; a Major Wound to the bird ends it and costs 1 FP. Will-4 after each episode or -1 to Influence rolls until a full night's sleep. Die while bonded and a fragment of you passes into the raven (+1 IQ, your attachments).
00004.name: Warg Dreams

00005.notes: Rank 1 = Menkhu (line-knower), one of some two hundred. Yargachin (priest) is Rank 2 and costs 5 more - that is what the cut buys, and it is deferred, not refused. Full value in the Neck; Social Engineering p.16 -1/3 outside it. B29-30
00005.name: Religious Rank 1

00006.notes: Free action, once per turn, before or after the maneuver: shift the spear between one- and two-handed grips, and/or into or out of a Defensive Grip (MA109-111). Buys the two-handed thrust (1d+1 imp instead of 1d, tripled at the vitals) and a standing +1 to Parry from the front, without ever spending a Ready. Does NOT cover the reach change - the * in the spear's Reach 1-2* is a separate Ready option (MA102). Specialised by weapon, so it does nothing for the bow, and nothing for the bow-to-spear swap; that is still Fast-Draw (Spear). DEPENDS on the buckler being strapped to the forearm rather than hand-gripped - RAW a buckler occupies a hand (B287) and this perk would be dead weight. Precedent for the strap: LTC2 p.19. Precedent for the perk on a spear fighter: MA Gladiators p.14, retiarius.
00006.name: Grip Mastery (Spear)

00007.notes: Kesmen (cut-lines), his native tongue, free. No written form - the language has no script. The Turchin are the people; Kesmen is what they speak.
00007.name: Language: Kesmen

00009.notes: Every night, privately, with the tashyar in his hand and the lines already on him. He has never broken skin. He has told no one.
00009.name: Rehearses the cut

00010.notes: He counts what is on another man's cord before he speaks to him, and everyone notices him doing it.
00010.name: Counts the horn-tips

00011.notes: He cannot put the cut in the future tense out loud. It is always 'if the Bashchin allows it,' never 'when.' Men have started to notice.
00011.name: Will not say 'when'

00012.notes: Asks what closed it, and does not like the answer when it is 'nothing.'
00012.name: Distrusts a clean scar

00013.notes: Aloud, unasked, to men who did not want to know. He cannot let a bad cut stand.
00013.name: Corrects the butchery

00014.notes: -3 reactions from the southern North, the northern riverlands and the Vale. Small class of people (x1/3), so 3 levels cost -5 points. The pair is one multifaceted Reputation netting 0. B26-28; People Affected
00014.name: Bad Reputation 3

00015.notes: Called to the grove when the herd is thin, when a Külyarga is wanted somewhere it has no business being performed, or when forty-one priests must stand in one place. He goes.; Frequency
00015.name: Duty (the Yarga)

00016.notes: The fifth yasakh: he may not name the opened, living or dead, ever again. He calls them by the wound, or by what he found inside them. B160
00016.name: Vow (Minor)

00017.notes: The first yasakh: nothing whole. He may put nothing into his body that has not been opened first by his own hand. The second yasakh (he may not eat the beast he opened, at the Ashkun) binds the officiant at the Qanyarga and is dormant until he is Yargachin. B132
00017.name: Disciplines of Faith (Ritualism)

00018.notes: The sixth yasakh: he may not sleep on hard ground. Turokh (the Earth) is underneath, and where the ground is hard he is not there to lie on. B160
00018.name: Vow (Major)

00020.notes: The third and fourth yasakh (that-which-is-forbidden): he may not open a body unasked, and he may not refuse a request to open a living body. Binds the opener, so it binds a Menkhu. Any character who says it aloud has compelled him. B160
00020.name: Vow (Great)

00005.notes: The -5 for lack of Physician is bought off by Esoteric Medicine (Menkhu) at 12+, which substitutes for Physician. LT p.11
00005.name: Surgery

00010.notes: Hard technique, default Spear-3, bought to the cap. Vitals is -3 to hit and triples impaling damage. B399
00010.name: Targeted Attack (Spear Thrust/Vitals) ([object Object])

00011.notes: Hard technique, default Bow-3 = 11, bought to the cap. Erases the vitals penalty on the opening shot; impaling triples at the vitals. B399
00011.name: Targeted Attack (Bow Shot/Vitals) ([object Object])

00012.notes: Finding the plants, and the leeches.
00012.name: Naturalist (Earthlike)

00013.notes: a successful Religious Ritual roll gives +2 to reactions when dealing with the faithful
00013.name: Religious Ritual (Turchin)

00016.notes: Dropped to 1 point on 2026-08-18 to pay for Grip Mastery (Spear). Surgery-14 and Esoteric Medicine (Menkhu)-15 cover the anatomy; nothing in canon turns on 14 vs 13 here.
00016.name: Professional Skill (Butcher)

00018.notes: The only close-work tool. Poison the point.
00018.name: Knife

00019.notes: Cuts one second off every reload. The bow is Shots 1(2).
00019.name: Fast-Draw (Arrow)

00020.notes: GM-approved specialty, B195. Works from a sling or rack, not the ground.
00020.name: Fast-Draw (Spear)

00000.situation: to Dodge, Parry & Block against attacks from the front or buckler side

00000.notes:
**TRANCE — the technologies of the sacred**
                                            
                                            How the Menkhu (line-knower) puts a mind under, and what comes back. Costs no points: every roll below is a skill he already owns.
        
        THIS IS AN EDIT
A gathering of scraped vellum in a hide cover, kept against the yarqap. Westerosi, because Kesmen (cut-lines) has no script — a small square hand that stopped improving at eleven.
00000.name: The Book of Metabackpacking

00001.notes: One horn from a Qanyarga, one tooth from a Külyarga. Nineteen years old, standing among men who sound like a bone-yard in a wind. Men count them before they speak.
00001.originalName: Horn-tip and tooth on a cord
00001.name: Horn-tip and tooth on a cord

00001.notes: Splitting-vessel — the hide roll of knapped stone tashyar he intends to cut himself with at Umakhtamar. Stone rather than bronze is practice, not prohibition; the metal ban was never law. ~1 lb.
00001.name: Yarqap

00002.notes: the aurochs-skull mask, cracked across the left orbit. Custom, no weight worth tracking        Issued, not owned — masks belong to the office. Under it he is not Störm but Turkes, and what he says cannot be held against him afterward.
00002.name: The Bosbash

00003.notes: Used to clean rot out of a wound that has already gone bad. The maggots eat dead flesh and stop at living flesh, which no blade can be trusted to do. Needs four days' notice to breed a fresh batch.        A lidded ox horn, kept damp, kept away from the food, never opened upwind. Blown on purpose by bog-flies onto a scrap of liver.        Nothing he carries is more orthodox — they open, and they are incapable of closing — and nothing empties a southern tent faster. Southerners let him do it exactly once.
00003.name: The maggot-horn

00004.notes: Used to draw blood and fluid up to the surface: deep bruising, a chest that will not clear, an abscess that will not come up. Warmed and set on the skin. Leeches do the same work wherever there is standing water.        A small ox horn with the tip cut open. A bruise raised on purpose over a deeper hurt.        Drawing out is the whole of his medicine. Everything he does to a body he can name; what the body does afterwards is the body's business, and he has decided, privately and without asking anyone, that it is not his.
00004.name: Cupping horn

00005.notes: Used to put the edge back on bronze and to press stone tools sharp again. Bronze is cold-worked hard with the pebble, not ground; the antler tine pressure-flakes stone.        A smooth river pebble and an antler tine, in one fold of hide.        The tine is for the other roll. Every night he takes out the tashyar (stone-splitter) he has not used, presses the edges up sharper than anything in the kesqap (cutting-vessel), and puts them away.        The quirk 'Rehearses the cut' has a physical object. This is it.
00005.name: Burnisher and tine

00006.notes: Used to straighten warped shafts, replace lost fletching, and reseat heads that have worked loose. Keeps thirty-five arrows flying true.        An antler shaft-wrench, spare fletching in gut, sinew, and a small pot of pine pitch kept hard and warmed at the fire.        Thirty-five barbed heads are thirty-five things nobody sells him. He straightens and refletches most evenings he is not doing something else, which is most evenings. A shaft that flies wide is a dose of belladonna lost in the mud.
00006.name: Arrow-kit

00007.notes: Used to mend and waterproof clothing, boots and hood. The tallow keeps hide and wool from rotting through; the wood-ash and stale water strips wool that has gone foul.        A bird-bone tube stoppered with wax: bone needles, sinew thread, spare hide thongs. A horn of rendered tallow beside it.        Hooded hide over wool that has been wet for a decade does not last a decade unattended. He greases it the way other men clean armour, and he is exact about it, and it still smells like the bog, because that is what it is.
00007.name: Needle-case, thongs, grease

00008.notes: belladonna and viper venom (5/5)        Belladonna allows no resistance roll on its first cycle. One dose per strike, or three blocked or parried; one per arrow. It only fires if the attack gets through DR.
00008.name: Poison doses in sealed gut

00009.notes: Used to pack and cover a dressed wound. The moss absorbs and keeps the wound sweet for a day and a night; the willow bark under it is chewed for pain and fever, the bog myrtle burned or rubbed on against flies. A Naturalist roll replaces the whole bag anywhere there is standing water.        Sphagnum, dried, in a net bag that weighs nothing and drinks four times its own weight.        All three grow within a mile of anywhere he has ever slept. It is the only medicine he owns that he has never had to ask a living man for, and he is unsentimental about the rest for exactly that reason.
00009.originalName: Bog moss, and the herb-gut under it
00009.name: Bog moss, and the herb-gut under it

00010.notes: Used to dress an open wound, laid on after the wine and under the moss. Does not spoil, ever, and so is the one medicine that keeps as long as the road does.        That-which-will-not-open. A hand's weight of it, going brown.        It does not rot, does not sour, does not part. A vessel of it opened after a hundred years is still honey — the most whole thing he has ever handled, and the best thing in the world to lay on an opened wound. He has never resolved that, and he does not raise it.        Under the 1st yasakh nothing whole enters him unopened, so every dose is cut with water or sour wine first, aloud, by name, before it touches a patient or his own mouth. It takes him longer than it takes anybody else. The men have started timing it.
00010.name: Yarilmaz — honey, sealed in gut

00011.notes: Used as travel rations. One cake is a day's walking. Keeps a season without spoiling and needs no cooking.        Dried eel, waterfowl and smoked hare pounded into rendered fat with bog cranberry and crowberry, pressed into cakes and wrapped in gut. Hard enough to have earned the name.        Under the 1st yasakh it cannot be eaten whole, so every cake is cut before it is eaten, always across the same line, and the halves are never laid back together on one board.
00011.name: Ashtash — food-stone

00012.notes: Used to wash a wound before anything else touches it, and to thin the honey to a working consistency. Drinkable at need.        Traded up out of the south and worth more than his knife.        It goes onto the wound first and it bites, and the biting is the point: it opens where it lands. What is left cuts the honey. What is left after that is drunk in mouthfuls too small to be hospitality.        The only medicine in the roll his doctrine has never had to argue with.
00012.originalName: Sour wine, in a stopped horn
00012.name: Sour wine, in a stopped horn

00013.notes: Used to keep the reflex bow dry and to replace a string that has stretched or parted. Three spares. A composite bow left wet comes apart at the glue and cannot be repaired in the field.        A greased hide sleeve. In a fold of it, three strings of twisted sinew carried against his skin under the wool where they stay dry, and a lump of beeswax cut with tallow to dress them.        A reflex bow is horn and sinew laid up with hide glue, and hide glue dissolves in water, and he lives in a bog. It comes out to be strung and goes back the moment it is not wanted. He watched a better bow than his come apart over one wet autumn and has not been casual since.
00013.name: Bow-case, spare strings, wax

00014.notes: Used to cut, probe, stitch and dress a living body. This is the surgical kit: without one, Surgery and Esoteric Medicine are improvised at -2 or worse (B424). It grants no bonus — its absence is the penalty.        Cutting-vessel, and not the yarqap (splitting-vessel). Bronze lancets, a bronze probe, a horn spoon, bone needles, sinew, boiled linen in a coil.        Bronze, because a bronze edge can be burnished hard again on a river stone in the field and knapped stone cannot be re-struck by firelight. The stone in the yarqap is for himself and has never touched anyone. This roll is for everyone else, and is opened most days.
00014.name: Kesqap

00015.notes: (10 Arrows)        Arrows he can reach without looking. Poisoned one at a time and kept apart, because a dose on the wrong shaft is a dose gone. Barbed - causes half the damage it took coming in when taken out.
00015.name: Quivers

00016.notes: Bronze. A tool, not an answer — 1d-2 either way. What he uses on a sentry now that the garrote is gone, and what he opens things with when the tashyar would be a blasphemy.
00016.name: Large Knife

00018.notes: Old bronze with an exterior of joined aurochs horns, tapering to rounded points, the central grip its widest part. DB 1 and another +1 to Block on top (LT116). Two pounds against a shield's fifteen — which is the whole reason he stays at No Encumbrance in a swamp.
00018.name: Parrying Buckler

00019.notes: Long and narrow bronze tip leather-fastened over the top of fire-hardened wood.
00019.name: Spear

00020.notes: Traded up the Bosyol from somewhere he could not name. Damage comes off the bow's rated ST and not his: thr+3 at ST 10 is 1d+1, two points more than the bow he carried before, for a quarter-pound. Three turns of Aim from cover, and an unaware man gets no defence at all.
00020.name: Reflex Bow

00021.notes: DR 1; Flexible, susceptible to blunt trauma; Holdout: -1.        Hooded hide over wool that has been wet for a decade. Bog-brown and undyed, the dress of the order rather than armour — it stops exactly one point of anything.; Torso
00021.name: Cloth, Padded

00000.notes: Used to comb out lice, and to dress his hair before walking into a camp that is not his.        Six teeth, two of them replacements.        A priest who arrives with his hair in ropes is a bog savage carrying a spear, and the office is worth more than his comfort. He combs at the tree line, before he is seen, not after.
00000.name: Antler comb

00001.notes: Used for surgery that needs a fire, a table and an hour: amputation, deep extraction, setting bone, sealing a bleed the linen will not stop. Too heavy and too slow for anything that happens on the track.        A bronze cautery rod, a small bow-saw for bone, split-cane splints, boiled linen by the yard, and a bronze bowl for catching what comes out.        The kesqap (cutting-vessel) on his hip is for what happens on the road. This is for what happens afterwards.        The cautery is in it and he dislikes that it is. A searing iron closes, and closing is the direction the world is not meant to travel. He has used it four times and named it aloud each time, which is not a rite anyone taught him either.
00001.name: The heavy roll

00001.notes: Used to refill the day-kit and the ration pouch. Bulk honey, wine, fat, salt and cakes against the remainder of the road — roughly forty days at current rate.        Honey in a sealed crock, a skin of sour wine, bog butter lifted out of the peat where it was buried a year ago and gone tangy, salt, and a sack of ashtash (food-stone).        What is on him is the day. This is the forty days.        It is not his. A priest cannot own or bequeath, and everything reverts to the grove, so drawing on it is an ulush (share / standing / worth) question — settled publicly, at the fire, and not by him.
00001.name: The stores

00000.situation: from members of your religion and those who respect your faith

00001.situation: from others aware of your reputation
